### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **4** package(s): `@objectstack/cli`, `@objectstack/core`, `@objectstack/runtime`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **153** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **5** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/cli/README.md`, `packages/runtime/src/index.ts`, `packages/spec/liveness/README.md`, …), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**16** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 12a1aba3a223032f2d6edd49bb54bab8d3a45924`.

⛔ **3** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **5** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/cli/README.md`, `packages/runtime/src/index.ts`, `packages/spec/liveness/README.md`, …) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** cross-cutting symbol(s) contributed no route anchor: `environmentId (38 routes)`
- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `os serve (command, 42 pages)`
- **23** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **58** of **210** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **185** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 12a1aba3a223032f2d6edd49bb54bab8d3a45924` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `eb7c7609c3e990a482c8a66686407ce5b6c71ec1` — the merge of head `af0b38885fe941d8478494385b47abbb069447ae` into base `12a1aba3a223032f2d6edd49bb54bab8d3a45924`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin eb7c7609c3e990a482c8a66686407ce5b6c71ec1 && git checkout eb7c7609c3e990a482c8a66686407ce5b6c71ec1
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 12a1aba3a223032f2d6edd49bb54bab8d3a45924 af0b38885fe941d8478494385b47abbb069447ae && git checkout -B drift-repro 12a1aba3a223032f2d6edd49bb54bab8d3a45924 && git merge --no-ff af0b38885fe941d8478494385b47abbb069447ae

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 12a1aba3a223032f2d6edd49bb54bab8d3a45924
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 12a1aba3a223032f2d6edd49bb54bab8d3a45924` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

So the TSDoc's "is not reached from a plugin's declared tier yet" is a measured sentence, not a hope. RIGHT.

It is a kernel-side consequence, not an authorable-key change, so `Metadata-protocol: none` stands; the core changeset discloses it in words.

2. **ADR-0025 v2 §3.6 is now stale in the same way**: "**nothing dispatches on the tier at load** — every plugin that loads today loads in-process" (L336), beside the already-carried §3.5 "Steps 4–7 do not exist" sentence, the §3.5 M1 ✅ line and the §7 dated note. ### ④ Design judgment

**`packages/spec/src/kernel/manifest.zod.ts`** — judged against ADR-0025 v2 §3.5 M1 and §3.6 (the tier table, "trust is default-deny", "M1 wires the dispatch point for T0 only; M3 routes `sandbox`"), ruling `6467932167` (slice 2 unchanged: the boot loader re-verifies against the store and refuses a key revoked since install), card item 5 ("replace with the M1 wording: `node` dispatched, others refused until M3"), and its first consumer, `installed-plugin-loader.ts#dispatchPluginRuntime` as `os serve` reaches it.

Every sentence of the new text, checked in the tree:

- "ENFORCED at load for a plugin `os plugin install` installed … the boot-time loader … `dispatchPluginRuntime` dispatches on the tier before it imports anything." HOLDS. `checkRecord` runs steps 2–4 (kept sha, signature over the raw bytes, tree byte-equal to the artifact, manifest id/version) and only then `dispatchPluginRuntime(manifest.runtime)`; `verifyInstalledPlugins` imports nothing; the import is in `loadInstalledPlugins`, for `verdict.verified` only. The `runtime` it dispatches on is read from the manifest **inside the signed, re-verified artifact**, not from the on-disk file, so a tier edited in the install directory is `tree_changed` before it is ever read as a tier. That is the right order: the dispatch cannot be steered by anything the signature does not cover.
- "`node` is imported in process with a full PluginContext — author code in the host process, T0, NOT isolation." HOLDS. `materializeStackPlugin(pathToFileURL(entry))` with a plain dynamic import, then `kernel.use` in `installed-plugins-boot.ts`; no enforcer scoping (that is M2, as the card says).
- "`sandbox` and `worker` are REFUSED by name until M3 routes them, with no in-process fallback." HOLDS. `dispatchPluginRuntime` returns `runtime_not_dispatched` for anything that is not `node` and not unset; the loader `refuse`s and never reaches the entry check or the import; `installed-plugins-boot.ts` prints the `✗` line and the banner counts it. The loader test asserts `imported == []` for both tiers; the serve integration test boots a real `os serve` with a `sandbox` plugin and asserts its marker file was never written.
- "an installed plugin that declares no tier is refused too (default-deny)." HOLDS: `runtime_undeclared` for `undefined`, `null` and `''`. Judged against §3.6's "Trust is default-deny … `node` is an opt-in privilege": refusing an unspoken tier rather than defaulting it to in-process is the only reading under which the sentence is true at a local boot. Right.
- "So a declared `sandbox` is never run unconfined: today it is not run at all." HOLDS, and this is the sentence that makes the describe honest where the old one was: the old text said the tier did not isolate; the new text does not claim isolation either, it says the unisolated path refuses.
- "The QuickJS runner … is not reached from a plugin's declared tier yet." HOLDS by census (①.5).
- "A plugin a stack's own `plugins` array names is the app's code and is not dispatched on this field." HOLDS: `serve.ts`'s config `plugins` loop (`kernel.use(pluginToLoad)`) takes modules and objects, reads no manifest, and runs before `registerInstalledPlugins`; those entries carry no `runtime` value to dispatch on.
- Both describes: "enforced at the cloud marketplace publish gate (… HTTP 422 …) and at boot for a locally installed plugin: only `node` is loaded (in process, not isolated); `sandbox` and `worker` are refused until … M3". Each clause is one of the sentences above; both halves of the split are still stated, as the pin requires and as the 2026-08-30 ruling that chose "say it truthfully" over retirement requires.
- Card acceptance "the listed self-descriptions are deleted in the same PRs; no new NOT ENFORCED prose is added": HOLDS. "Load-side enforcement is NOT implemented", "nothing dispatches on the tier", "not a candidate … until it lands" are gone; the retracted sentence is pinned absent; nothing new says "NOT ENFORCED".

Break attempts, each against the live tree:

- **Reach the import without saying `node`.** A record whose on-disk manifest says `node` but whose artifact says `sandbox`: the loader reads the artifact's manifest, so `runtime_not_dispatched`; and the edited file is `tree_changed` first. A record installed with `--trust-unsigned` declaring `sandbox`: unsigned skips step 3 only; step 5 still refuses. A plugin registered through the host's `kernel.use` from the config `plugins` array: not "a locally installed plugin" in the text's sense, and the TSDoc says so. None makes the text false.
- **Load a `node` plugin somewhere the dispatch is not consulted.** The only production caller of `loadInstalledPlugins` is `installed-plugins-boot.ts`, reached from `serve.ts` on both the standalone (`shouldBootWithLibrary`) and host-config paths after the `plugins` loop (`os dev` / `os start` spawn `serve`); a programmatic `@objectstack/runtime` boot never loads installed plugins at all, so the claim "only `node` is loaded" is vacuously true there, never false.
- **Make `dispatchPluginRuntime` accept a near-miss.** `'Node'`, `'node '`, `['node']` all fall to `runtime_not_dispatched` (strict `===`); `ManifestSchema` would refuse them at build anyway.
- **Text vs ADR table.** §3.6's T0 row says "In-process dynamic `import`; full `PluginContext` gated by declared capabilities" — the "gated by declared capabilities" half is M2 (§3.7 "registered only today"); the hits file does not claim it (it says "full PluginContext", unqualified by grants), so it does not overclaim against the ADR.

Findings on the hits file:

- **Should-fix (small):** the describe strings say "a locally installed plugin" without naming `os plugin install` as the install path, and the carve-out for a stack's own `plugins` array lives only in the TSDoc. A reader of the generated reference page (which renders the describe alone) could read "locally installed" as "any plugin on this machine". One clause ("a plugin `os plugin install` installed") in both describes would close it; the pin's three probes still match after that edit.
- **Should-fix (small):** the field TSDoc keeps "Unset implies a pure-metadata package (no executable code)" two lines above text that now says an installed plugin with no tier is refused. Both are true (every `.osplugin` `os plugin build` produces is code-bearing, so "unset" on an installed artifact is an omission, not a metadata-only package), but the two sentences sit together without the bridge; one clause would do.
- **No must-fix.** The describe tells the truth about which tier dispatches (`node`, in process, not isolated), which are refused (`sandbox`, `worker`, unset) and where (the boot of `os serve` for `os plugin install`-installed plugins), and the gate that keeps it true (`plugin-runtime-tier-truthful-text.test.ts`) moved in the same change.
